fact: UNCDF's assessment says citizens open bank and mobile money accounts by presenting national IDs, but Burundi has no national identity database to support financial institutions in KYC checks, so account-opening KYC is not checked against an ID register.
system: Bank and mobile money account-opening KYC

fact: Agence Ecofin reports ARCT's communique of 3 June 2026 requiring Burundian mobile subscribers to regularise SIM identification by 25 June 2026 or have lines deactivated, with only the carte nationale d'identite accepted for the operation, under a ministerial ordinance of 13 January 2026.

Connecting Africa reports mandatory SIM and eSIM registration in Burundi began in mid-June 2026, requiring registrants to present legible, up-to-date identification documents at a registration point, with ARCT interconnecting operators and state bodies for real-time monitoring of registration and user identity.

The Bank of the Republic of Burundi's Deputy Governor says a contract was signed in November 2024 for a central bank biometric financial ID system, with testing planned on two commercial banks and two mobile money operators.

The article reports the Master Plan for the Digitalization of Public Services (PDDSP 2023-2033) as noting the absence of verifiable digital ID systems in Burundi, and recommending an e-signature and authentication infrastructure.
